'''''Passiflora mixta''''', from the family [[Passifloraceae]] is also known as '''''curuba''''' (in [[Colombia]]), '''''curuba de indio''''', '''''curuba de monte''''', '''''curubita''''', '''''parcha''''' (in [[Venezuela]]), and ''taxo'' (in [[Ecuador]]). Originally, it derived from the [[monophyletic]] ''Passiflora'' subgenus ''[[Banana passionfruit|Tacsonia]]''. ''Passiflora mixta'' is endemic to the [[Americas]]. A perennial [[vine]], the ''Passiflora mixta'' is pink to orange-red in color.<ref name=":0">{{cite web |last= d'Eeckenbrugge |first= Geo Coppens |title= Fruits from America |url= http://ciatweb.ciat.cgiar.org/ipgri/fruits_from_americas/frutales/Ficha%20Passiflora%20mixta.htm |agency= CIRAD-FLHOR/IPGRI |publisher= Project for Neotropical Fruits |access-date= 2017-02-27 |archive-date= 2016-03-05 |archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20160305124623/http://ciatweb.ciat.cgiar.org/ipgri/fruits_from_americas/frutales/Ficha%20Passiflora%20mixta.htm |url-status= dead }}</ref>

== Description ==
[[File:Passiflora mixta flowers and leaves.jpg|thumb|left|Ecuador, Napo Province, [[Papallacta]]]]
''Passiflora mixta'' can be identified by its large pink flowers and trilobate [[coricaeous]] leaves, which are tubular in shape and protrude from its branches. It has a hairy elongated [[bract]] and {{cvt|7|-|15|cm |in|adj=mid| long}} [[hypanthium]] (flower tube) that contains a narrow nectar chamber. The [[Ovary (botany)|ovaries]], [[anther]]s, and [[Stigma (botany)|stigma]]s are located anterior to the hypanthium near the [[androgynophore]]. The species is capable of producing fruits and flowers that remain open for 3 to 5 days by producing half-pendant, horizontal, or erect flowers.
 
The species is wild, collected, and an important genetic resource for [[banana passionfruit]] breeding.<ref name=":1">{{cite journal |last=Lindberg |first=Annika Buèchert |last2=Olesen |first2=Jens Mogens |title=The fragility of extreme specialization |journal= Journal of Tropical Ecology |year=2001 |volume=17 |pages=323–329 |doi=10.1017/s0266467401001213}}</ref>

=== Morphology ===
* Stem{{snd}}Sub five-angular
* Leaf pubescence{{snd}}Not present on the upper surface; however, missing to seldom dense on the lower surface
* [[Stipule]]s are moderate to large in size, 6–20 mm in length, 12–30 mm wide ({{cvt|12|-|30|mm|disp=out}}), [[Reniform leaf|reniform]], [[Dentate leaf|dentate]] or serrate, persistent
* [[Peduncle (botany)|Peduncles]] are robust with a varied length, resulting in half-pendent, horizontal, or erect flowers
* The bracts are joined for half their length or more
* The [[petal|corolla]] color ranges from pale pink to intense red, and is [[campanulate]] (bell-shaped)
* The floral tube to [[sepal]] ratio is 1.6:2.6, and the nectar chamber is slightly broader than the floral tube
* At maturity, the [[pericarp]] often appears green, occasionally turning yellow; [[aril]]s are scarce, and grey to orange in color.
<ref>{{cite web |last= d'Eeckenbrugge |first=Coppens |title= Passiflora tarminiana |url=http://www.hear.org/pier/species/passiflora_tarminiana.htm}}</ref>

== Pollination ==
This species of ''Passiflora'' is pollinated by the [[sword-billed hummingbird]] (''Ensifera ensifera''), which is the only living species in its genus. The hummingbird is found throughout the northern [[Andes]] and is identified by its extremely long beak, longer than its entire body. The long beak allows the bird to reach nectar at the bottom of the plant's long corolla tubes.<ref>{{cite web |title=Why Evolution is True |date=27 November 2010 |url=http://whyevolutionistrue.wordpress.com/2010/11/27/the-beakiest-bird/ |accessdate= 16 May 2011}}</ref>{{Better source needed|reason=The current source is likely insufficiently reliable (blog? [[WP:NOTRS]]).|date=May 2024}}

== Distribution ==
''Passiflora mixta'' ranges from Venezuela to [[Bolivia]], and has been naturalized in [[Africa]] and [[New Zealand]]. It is restricted to [[highland]] areas between {{cvt|1,700|and|3,700|m}} above sea level. The species can withstand disturbances and is more prominent in dryer environments and lower altitudes than other species of ''Tacsonia''. It grows along the edges of forests and along the margins.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":1" /><ref>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 December 2017}}</ref>
